title: The office view of Capitol and his golf murals
summary: Willard observes the view onto the old Capitol Records building and Lee's golf murals; he declines to discuss the jazz label further.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I think it was kind of interesting, you were talking about back during the record band and Capitol was right over there, and I wasn't sitting close enough to the window to see, here on the 17th floor, of the United California Bank Building -- I wasn't sitting close enough to the window to be able to realize when you gestured that way, you are in a position here so that you can look down right on top of the building that was Capitol Records.

I mean you can look down on RCA from where I'm sitting, but over there you can see the front door of what used to be Capitol Records, and the back door. And here in your office, which is decorated by giant photo murals of golf courses.
Of Pebble Beach and Monterey Peninsula. That's the 18th hole at Pebble Beach, and that's the 16th hole at Monterey Peninsula.
I bought them from a guy up north. His name slips by, but I think they are great pictures, you know?
Oh, they're beautiful. You're a That's a golfball ashtray golf man, right?
Yeah, golf is my thing. I enjoy that. Anything more?
Not unless you want to talk about your specific plans for ... the jazz label.
I don't think so. I'll wait to see if it happens. If it happens, then I will have plenty to say about it.
